description: A collection of learning resources for curious software engineers

summary.one_liner: A curated, opinionated link and book list of learning resources for software engineers, covering programming craft, career growth, and many technical topics.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome"-style list rather than a software project: a long README of links, book recommendations, and short annotated summaries of articles, talks, and courses. It is organized as a table of contents with sections on principles, must-read books and articles, and then many topic sections such as algorithms, API design, databases, code reviews, debugging, career growth, and AI/LLM topics. Entries are marked with emoji for lists, books, videos, slides, must-reads, and papers. The author states the list is intentionally concise and not comprehensive. The README is truncated in the provided text, so later sections (such as incident response, testing, and others listed in the table of contents) were not fully reviewed.
use_cases: Finding must-read books for software engineers
Looking up career advice for senior and staff engineers
Studying algorithms and data structures resources
Reading about database internals and Postgres practices
Finding code review and debugging best practices
notable: Opinionated curation of books, articles, and talks for software engineers
Organized by a long topic table of contents, from algorithms to career growth
Includes a dedicated section on agentic coding and LLM-related reading
Links to free computer science courses such as MIT's Missing Semester and SICP
caveats: The author states the list is deliberately not comprehensive and is kept short
Selections are opinionated and the author does not endorse every line of every resource
Some referenced books are paid, such as The Imposter's Handbook at $30
